summary: Serialize Transform _transform work so the next chunk is not processed until callback completes.

target.notes: Node never calls _transform in parallel; the callback gates dequeuing of the next input. callback(error) fails the stream; callback(null, data) can emit output equivalently to push(data) then callback().

semantics.output: zero or more pushes / optional callback data
semantics.error: callback error enters stream error path

caveats: Application code must not call _transform directly.
Do not map each chunk to independent Task.Run work; that can reorder chunks.

tests.name: second transform waits
tests.input: const {Transform}=require('node:stream'); const calls=[]; let first; const t=new Transform({transform(c,e,cb){calls.push(c.toString()); if(!first)first=cb; else cb(null,c)}}); t.write('a'); t.write('b'); console.log(calls.join(',')); first(null,Buffer.from('a'));
tests.expected_behavior: before first callback prints only a; b is processed afterward
